messages.subject: Uncertainty in INLA models and selecting new sample sites
parts:
Hi INLA community!

Follow-up question to a previous post in this conversation - is there a way to parse out from the posterior variance that INLA outputs, an understanding of what regions of uncertainty are being driven by epistemic uncertainty (uncertainty in the INLA model) vs aleatoric (variability in the data). I'm interested in looking at selecting new sample sites that would hopefully improve the model fit and get us more accurate estimates of the hyperparameters and regressino coefficients, for an LGCP model. I'm struggling to understand the meaning of the outputted variance

Thanks

Jess

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Uncertainty in INLA models and selecting new sample sites
parts:
I think "uncertainty in the INLA model" needs to be defined more precisely. INLA is a method/algorithm for Bayesian computation. The statistical model set (for INLA to compute from) has epistemic uncertainty.

The Bayesian hierarchical models include three levels of probability distributions. Thus, measuring its epistemic uncertainty is not easy. Let's make it simpler so we can start getting something.

Consider the most simple geostatistical model, the (double)-Gaussian case where the data, given the process, is assumed Gaussian and the process is also Gaussian. Furthermore, assume no prior with inference based on the likelihood. Given the Gaussian process distribution assumption and the process parameters known there are classic expressions. These are useful to get a hint about this. See attached a screenshot from the "Model Based Geostatistics" book (although a similar formula can also be found in the "Mixed Models" literature).

Is this the direction you want to go?

best,
Elias
